processing: Fully oxidised orthodox black tea, sold in broken grades such as FBOP as well as under plain estate labels.
harvest_season: No garden-specific calendar could be confirmed; as with other Assam gardens, the May to June second flush is generally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Dark brown broken leaf, typical of a broken Assam grade.
appearance_liquor: Deep reddish amber, as is usual for second-flush Assam.
appearance_wet: Small coppery pieces of leaf, typical of a broken grade.
taste_profile: Malty and full-bodied, as is typical of second-flush Assam; no independent tasting record could be confirmed.

brewing.notes: A broken grade gets strong quickly: start at three minutes. It takes milk well.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and grade, usually from the current or previous season, with the second-flush FBOP as the best-known lot. As with other Assam black teas, it is meant for drinking within a year or two rather than ageing.
description:
Borengajuli is an Assam garden in Udalguri, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, in the belt of estates near the Bhutan border.

It turns up mostly as a broken-leaf orthodox tea. That small leaf gives colour and strength quickly, and in Assam the May to June picking generally carries the most body.

Expect a plain, sturdy, malty cup. Too long a steep brings out sharpness, so begin at three minutes and add milk if you like it that way. This is breakfast tea with a known address.

When buying, look for the flush, grade and season on the label. The estate name alone tells you little, because quality moves from one picking to the next.
history:
Little is documented about when the garden was planted or by whom. A 2014 trade blog places it near the village of Bamonjuli and describes it as part of the McLeod Russel group; ownership may have changed since.

The area it sits in was part of old Darrang district before Udalguri became a district of its own in 2004, so older writing may place these gardens differently.
